lines.text: How does your phone know exactly where you are?

phrases.text: How does your phone know exactly where you are?

lines.text: The answer is falling from space, and the strangest part involves Einstein.

phrases.text: The answer is falling from space,
and the strangest part involves Einstein.

lines.text: About thirty-one GPS satellites orbit the Earth, some twenty thousand kilometers up.

phrases.text: About thirty-one GPS satellites orbit the Earth,
some twenty thousand kilometers up.

lines.text: Each one laps the planet about twice a day.

phrases.text: Each one laps the planet about twice a day.

lines.text: They carry atomic clocks on board.

phrases.text: They carry atomic clocks on board.

lines.text: They constantly broadcast where they are, and the exact time.

phrases.text: They constantly broadcast where they are,
and the exact time.

lines.text: Your phone never transmits back. It only listens.

phrases.text: Your phone never transmits back.
It only listens.

lines.text: Those signals reach you in about seven hundredths of a second.

phrases.text: Those signals reach you in about seven hundredths of a second.

lines.text: But light covers about thirty centimeters in a billionth of a second.

phrases.text: But light covers about thirty centimeters in a billionth of a second.

lines.text: Off by a millionth of a second, and you'd miss by three hundred meters.

phrases.text: Off by a millionth of a second,
and you'd miss by three hundred meters.

lines.text: One satellite's delay puts you somewhere on a giant sphere.

phrases.text: One satellite's delay puts you somewhere on a giant sphere.

lines.text: A second satellite, and the two spheres meet in a circle.

phrases.text: A second satellite,
and the two spheres meet in a circle.

lines.text: A third narrows it to two points, one of them usually far out in space.

phrases.text: A third narrows it to two points,

lines.text: A fourth fixes your phone's own clock, which is nowhere near atomic.

phrases.text: A fourth fixes your phone's own clock,

lines.text: Now the strangest part: Einstein is in your pocket.

phrases.text: Now the strangest part:
Einstein is in your pocket.

lines.text: Up there, weaker gravity makes their clocks run faster, by about forty-five microseconds a day.

phrases.text: Up there, weaker gravity makes their clocks run faster,
by about forty-five microseconds a day.

lines.text: Their speed slows them by about seven. So they gain thirty-eight every day.

phrases.text: Their speed slows them by about seven.

lines.text: Left uncorrected, GPS would drift about ten kilometers every day.

phrases.text: Left uncorrected,

lines.text: So engineers tune the clocks to tick slower before launch, and the dot stays on you.
